chapters.title: Short 1: Stop building one giant AI agent

cues.text: Your AI agent is doing way too much. Here's the fix.
cues.note: Hook: "1 AGENT, 7 JOBS" slams in over the overloaded red agent box.

cues.text: The problem, the fix, and the one line of code that does it.
cues.note: Three pills: Problem · Fix · Code.

cues.text: Picture an online store assistant. One agent saves the customer's details, lists products, adds to the cart, removes items, confirms the cart, and places the order.
cues.note: Tool chips fly out of the single agent, one per tool named.

cues.text: That's seven tools and one giant instruction.
cues.note: "7 tools · 1 giant instruction" badge; the box turns red.

cues.text: As it grows, it starts picking the wrong tool, and it's really hard to test.
cues.note: A wrong tool chip flashes; the box shakes with an OVERLOADED tag.

cues.text: The fix: split the work. One root agent, like a front desk, and three sub-agents: catalog, cart and order.
cues.note: The same box turns blue and rises as ROOT; three sub-agents drop in below.

cues.text: Each tool moves to the agent that's responsible for it.
cues.note: The tool chips fly to their owners.

cues.text: In Google ADK, that's one line: sub_agents equals a list of your agents.
cues.note: Code card: sub_agents=[catalog_agent, cart_agent, order_agent].

cues.text: Want the full build? Watch the full video, linked below.
cues.note: End card: "Full video ↓" with the main video's title.

chapters.title: Short 2: How AI agents hand off a conversation

cues.text: How does one AI agent hand a customer to another?
cues.note: Hook: a white pulse jumps between two agent boxes.

cues.text: It comes down to three things: descriptions, one built-in tool, and a shared session.
cues.note: Three numbered cards stack in.

cues.text: First, every agent has a description. The LLM reads them to decide who should answer next.
cues.note: Card 1: description quotes appear under each agent; the LLM scans them and picks one.

cues.text: Second, as soon as you add sub-agents, Google ADK gives your agents a tool called transfer_to_agent.
cues.note: Card 2: the transfer_to_agent(...) chip.

cues.text: Calling it hands control to another agent: down to a sub-agent, sideways to a sibling, or back up to the parent.
cues.note: The pulse travels down, sideways, then back up the tree with labels.

cues.text: Only one agent is in control at a time.
cues.note: IN CONTROL tag; the other agents dim.

cues.text: Third, they all share one session. Same history, same state. Nothing gets lost when control moves.
cues.note: Card 3: one session slab under all four agents.

cues.text: Watch the full video, linked below.
cues.note: End card: "Full video ↓".

chapters.title: Short 3: The parameter your AI never sees

cues.text: There's a parameter in your ADK tools that the AI never sees.
cues.note: Hook: the function signature with tool_context blurred, then revealed.

cues.text: What it is, why it's there, and the one mistake to avoid.
cues.note: Three pills: What · Why · The mistake.

cues.text: It's called tool_context. When the LLM calls save customer details, it only sees name, email and phone.
cues.note: "What the LLM sees" card: name, email, phone.

cues.text: ADK hides tool_context from the model, then passes it in when the tool runs. It spots it by its type hint, ToolContext.
cues.note: "What your function gets" card: tool_context added by ADK.

cues.text: Through it, your tool reaches the session. Read state like a dictionary: state dot get. Write it the same way: state, key, equals value.
cues.note: READ / WRITE code lines.

cues.text: ADK saves every write to the session.
cues.note: The write flows into an amber session.state box.

cues.text: The mistake? Changing a dictionary in place isn't saved. Always assign it back.
cues.note: Red ✕ on cart["P-101"] = 1, green ✓ on tool_context.state["cart"] = cart.

cues.text: The full walkthrough is in my full video, linked below.
cues.note: End card: "Full video ↓".

chapters.title: Short 4: Watch the state grow across 4 AI agents

cues.text: Four AI agents, one shopping trip, and one notebook they all share.
cues.note: Hook: four agent boxes around one amber notebook.

cues.text: Let's watch the session state grow, one agent at a time.
cues.note: An empty state panel: { }.

cues.text: Asha shares her name, email and phone. The root agent saves three keys, then hands her to the catalog agent, which adds a cart.
cues.note: user_name, user_email, user_phone appear; pulse to catalog; the cart key appears.

cues.text: The cart agent edits it, then sends her back to the catalog for a charger, and back again.
cues.note: The cart value updates; the pulse goes back and forth.

cues.text: When she's happy, it saves the total and marks the cart confirmed.
cues.note: cart_total and cart_confirmed appear.

cues.text: The order agent already knows her email and phone, because it reads them from state, and it adds the order ID and status.
cues.note: The email and phone rows glow blue (read); order_id and order_status appear.

cues.text: Eight keys, four agents, one shared session. Watch the full video, linked below.
cues.note: All 8 keys lit, tagged by agent; end card "Full video ↓".

chapters.title: Short 5: Run a multi-agent app in four commands

cues.text: Run a multi-agent AI app in four commands.
cues.note: Hook: a big "4" next to a terminal.

cues.text: Set up, install, add your key, and run.
cues.note: Four step pills.

cues.text: One: python dash m venv dot venv. That's a virtual environment, so this project's packages stay separate.
cues.note: Step 1: python -m venv .venv; a .venv folder appears.

cues.text: Activate it: dot venv, Scripts, activate on Windows, or source dot venv slash bin slash activate on Mac and Linux.
cues.note: The Windows and Mac/Linux activate commands; the prompt shows (.venv).

cues.text: Two: pip install dash r requirements dot txt.
cues.note: Step 2: pip install -r requirements.txt.

cues.text: Three: put your Gemini API key in a dot env file.
cues.note: Step 3: .env with GOOGLE_API_KEY=…

cues.text: Four: adk web. Open localhost 8000, and watch the State tab.
cues.note: Step 4: adk web; the State tab with the final state.

cues.text: The full step-by-step is in my full video, linked below.
cues.note: End card: "Full video ↓".
